newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on Sparks estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on Sparks estimate.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a wheat estimate by Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies, traders said.

Sources said Sparks estimated 1997 U.S. total wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels, above USDA's July outlook for 2.431 billion. Also Sparks tabbed 1997-98 U.S. wheat ending stocks at 861 million bushels, above USDA's July forecast for ending stocks at 650 million, sources said.
Sparks officials were unavailable for comment on the estimates.
Wheat futures also were hit by a drop in corn and soy, a technical slide plus slow exports, traders said.
"It was technically weakened yesterday anyway, then Sparks came out and there is no business around so down it went," a trader said.

News Morocco postponed a tender for 130,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat was cited. But European traders early Tuesday said Morocco set a retender for August 12 for 90,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat.
CBOT SRW wheat closed 1-1/4 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with September down 1-1/2 at $3.53-1/4.
Commercial buying underpinned prices, sources noted. Cargill Inc was a key purchaser of 4.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread dealings, FIMAT Futures did one million bushels of December/September at 15 cents, premium December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 22,000 contracts, below the 25,418 traded Monday.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 1500 December $4.00 puts at 41-1/4 to 42 cents, sold 600 Decewmber $3.70 puts at 21 to 21-3/4 cents, bought 500 September $3.50 calls at eight cents and bought 500 September $3.50 puts at seven cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, above the 5,093 traded Monday.
